reforms.description: Japan's structural reform programme concentrates public R&D funds on four priority areas—life sciences, information technology, environment, and nanotechnology—while introducing competition mechanisms to foster world-class universities. The government's FY 2002 fiscal plan prioritizes increased spending on science and technology, lifting expenditures by 2 trillion yen as part of a broader reallocation of spending priorities.
reforms.package_name: Japan Structural Reform Programme for Science and Technology (2001–2002)
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Concentrating public R&D on high-priority sectors (life sciences, IT, environment, nanotechnology) and increasing overall science spending supports productivity growth and innovation capacity. Competition mechanisms in universities enhance allocative efficiency.
reforms.status_evidence: Description [0] states the programme 'includes' focus on priority areas (present tense, announced); description [1] refers to FY 2002 plan as 'prioritizes' (future orientation). Most advanced status is announced.
reforms.importance_rationale: Structural reform programme with system-wide reallocation of 2 trillion yen across multiple priority sectors and introduction of competition mechanisms represents a major policy shift.
reforms.source_quote: The areas include environmental issues, coping with an ageing population, developing local facilities to fit regional needs, revitalising cities, promoting science and technology, cultivating human resources, and developing IT.

reforms.description: Japan established the Council for Science and Technology Policy under the Cabinet Office in January 2001 to increase emphasis on basic research and improve efficiency of public technology spending.
reforms.package_name: Council for Science and Technology Policy (2001)
reforms.component_name: Council for Science and Technology Policy establishment
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Establishing a dedicated policy council to increase emphasis on basic research and improve efficiency of public R&D spending enhances the governance and allocation of research resources, supporting long-term innovation capacity.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states the Council was 'established' in January 2001, indicating implementation.
reforms.importance_rationale: Creation of a new institutional body for science and technology policy coordination is significant but narrower in scope than a system-wide structural reform.
reforms.source_quote: Increase emphasis on basic research and improve efficiency of public technology spending. Council for Science and Technology Policy was established under the Cabinet Office in January 2001.

reforms.description: Japan revised its patent law to allow patent attorneys to play a greater role as specialists in intellectual property rights, enhancing the legal framework for technology commercialisation.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Strengthening the role of patent attorneys and enhancing the IP legal framework reduces transaction costs and barriers to technology commercialisation, supporting the conversion of research into market-ready innovations.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states Japan 'revised' its patent law, indicating the reform is in force.
reforms.importance_rationale: A targeted reform to the patent law framework is incremental and narrowly focused on IP specialist roles, not a system-wide change.
reforms.source_quote: Revise the patent law. Revised law for patent attorney in force since January 2001. It allows them to play a greater role as a specialist for the trade of intellectual property rights.

reforms.description: Japan liberalised venture capital markets by allowing three competing venture security markets to operate in full, with recommendations to improve market principles, disclosure rules, and IPO qualification procedures.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Liberalising venture capital markets and improving market governance (disclosure, IPO procedures) reduces barriers to startup financing and scaling, supporting the commercialisation of innovative firms.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states markets were 'allowed to operate in full', indicating implementation.
reforms.importance_rationale: Liberalisation of venture capital markets with multiple competing platforms is a significant structural change to the startup ecosystem, though narrower than economy-wide R&D reform.
reforms.source_quote: Encourage more start-ups and venture business operation. Three competing venture security markets now in full operation.
